The Omni Homestead Resort and Spa | Hotel in Hot Springs

The Omni Homestead Resort and Spa

The Omni Homestead Resort and Spa has been delighting vacationers including 24 U.S. presidents for over 250 years. Our one of a kind resort in Hot Springs, VA features a two acre water park and top ranked golf courses including the nations oldest first tee in continuous use. Deepen the experience with a soothing massage at The Spa at Omni Homestead. Enjoy local favorites at eight charming restaurants and bars and taste wines from fine regional vintners. However you choose to spend your Hot Springs vacation at The Omni Homestead Resort and Spa it is guaranteed to be memorable.

House policy

Check-in Time: 16:00 Check-out Time: 11:00 Cancel policy

All reservations must be cancelled before 12 noon local hotel time 3 days prior to arrival to avoid a cancellation charge. Individual rate plans, special events and high demand periods may have cancellation requirements that vary from the standard policy. Check specific rate description for complete details.


Travel with others

Children policyChildren up to 17 years of age and younger may stay free in same room with parents using existing bedding. If meals or amenities are included, there may be an additional charge.

Pets are allowed upon request

Two dogs are allowed, per reservation, when a valid credit card is on file. Our pet policy extends only to dogs. Other pets, including extreme or wild animals, are not allowed. Each room with a dog will be charged a one-time non-refundable fee of 200.00 USD. There will also be a per night fee of 50.00 USD per dog. Dogs left alone in the room must be in a cage or carrier. In the event that your pet is the cause of guest noise complaints, you will be asked to remove the pet and will be liable for financial compensation to those guests disturbed. You will be given an opportunity to respond to any noise complaints and in the event, you are unable to satisfy this request, you may be asked to leave property and will be financially responsible for any and all costs associated with appeasing complaints. Service animals for the blind or otherwise disabled are exempt from our pet policy. Dogs whose sole function is to provide comfort and companionship do not qualify for this exemption under ADA guidelines. Please note that only registered dogs are permitted at the resort.

Sherry Smith 2 years ago – Google

6

The resort is beautiful but I get the impression it is almost too big to maintain and is more reminiscent of a past time. The golf was challenging, the course in good shape, and it was not crowded. We took a well maintained and marked hike and took advantage of the pool (which had too many chaises too close together). Both on site dining restaurants were perfect for dinner and walking the grounds after dinner was pleasant.


Lee Ann Baer 2 years ago – Google

10

We had a wonderful stay at the homestead for our family vacation!y husband, 1 year old daughter and myself stayed in a beautiful room and enjoyed all of the amenities! The pool was great and our daughter really enjoyed the little splash pool and sand box perfect for younger kids! My husband played the main golf course there and said it was great! Also, all the food was wonderful; we especially enjoyed Jefferson’s and the breakfast buffet! And the afternoon tea with the piano in the grand lobby was a great every afternoon! I would definitely recommend this resort for couples and families alike!


Kim Flados 2 years ago – Google

7

The resort was absolutely beautiful! Our room was nice and had a great sleeping bed. A good little drive for us 6 1/2 hours. My only complaint is the restaurants on site are more than we want to spend. We had lunch at the outdoors pool area and had all other meals off site. We stayed 5 nights. Had a great time and loved the mountain setting.


Julie Albritton 2 years ago – Google

8

A family friendly resort with activities for all. Resort has beautiful scenery as well as history. Great place for a family vacation for all ages. Be sure to make a spa appointment and this will reserve you a spot by the spa pool and mineral pool...you will not have access without a reservation or by buying a day pass. (Adult only pool).


steve ricks 2 years ago – Google

5

Homestead is a wonderful place. The setting is probably one of the most beautiful in the world. The Cascades golf course is without compare. Our visits to the Spa have been less than great. Nothing terrible, but it is just not a high end spa and they charge high end prices. It is a bit of a disconnect. Food all over the resort is very good. Service is great. Staff does a great job.


Barbara Sloan 2 years ago – Google

10

Our group of 12 family members had a wonderful 5 day stay in July. Staff are wonderful and prompt. Highest ratings for the staff. We booked the spa and a number of resort activities and all were very enjoyable with knowledgeable and friendly guides. Our rooms were clean; pools were clean and well maintained; the grounds are beautiful, as is the building itself, with many areas to explore. I would not give five stars to the restaurants--menus are limited and the food was good but not excellent, perhaps due to high volume. We were there during the week and did not feel it was crowded. We had heard summers are very crowded, but perhaps just on weekends. This resort is a great luxury (though not the highest one can find) experience. We felt the service and amenities were worth the prices.


Emma 2 years ago – Google

10

Stayed here with family and was not at all disappointed! The pool is lovely, the golf courses (I'm told) are fantastic, staff is accommodating and friendly, and the grounds are absolutely gorgeous! Plenty of kids here seemed happy, as did adults, so it's fun for all ages! Would highly recommend, I had an absolutely lovely time here. There were even fireworks for Fiesta Friday!


Aymeric de Vazeille 2 years ago – Google

7

It is a very beautiful place. The rooms are a bit dated but the decor has a beautiful southern charm and is very authentic. BUT the service was slow when we were there and they do tend to nickel and dime you. If you go, make sure you get the "package" deals. And do go to the local restaurants. Some of them are really worth it (especially the ones associated with B&Bs)


Matt Angelelli 2 years ago – Google

9

It has been about 12 years since we visited the Homestead. It is much nicer than we previously remember. All of the activities we participated in were first rate. It is important to put an itinerary together early including dining reservations. We were able to put our ballroom dance lessons to use during dinner in the main dining room. We could not get over all of the happy families. The staff were great. We are looking to go back next year. We did horseback riding, archery, golf on both courses, zip lining, hiking, kayaking, dancing, and the pools. There were all great.

Matt


Anna B 2 years ago – Google

4

The Homestead is a beautiful property - we enjoyed our stay and most of the staff is spectacular. Sadly, money was taken from my wallet, which was inside my purse, closed in my suitcase and my experience with security 'rained on my otherwise, wonderful stay. (Yes, I should have used the safe, but this is my take on The Homestead.) So! Yes - visit it, stand firm on your reservation times regardless of what staff says when you call. Lock up you belongings. Avoid The Jefferson and Enjoy the Spa! It's a little slice of heaven.


Lee Drummond 2 years ago – Google

10

Beautiful resort with friendly staff, delicious food, gorgeous views, and so much to do. We felt particularly grateful for all of the kids’ activities. Thank you for making it so family-friendly (but still classy). We felt very welcomed and enjoyed every moment of our weekend getaway.


Zofia Smardz 2 years ago – Google

10

We had a wonderful time at the Homestead. I'm writing specifically to say a great big Thank You to Sandy in housekeeping, who was so helpful in finding and retrieving an item that one of our party had left behind in her room after we checked out. Sandy was extremely patient in fielding my repeated calls over several days to inquire about the item and to suggest places to look. Our story had a happy ending, and it's all due to her. So THANK YOU, Sandy. You are a credit to your job and to the Homestead. It's people like you who really make a place special. The Homestead is lucky to have you!


Judith Hammerschmidt 2 years ago – Google

9

The Homestead remains one of the loveliest of hotels in America. Nestled in the mountains, the view from every window soothes and amazes. The rooms are classic -- beautifully appointed, well maintained and large! They are rivaled only by the personal nature of the service. Each staff member is pleasant, helpful and prompt. I don't remember the last time we had such service, especially because this staff goes to great length to be welcoming. We were at The Homestead for a wedding, and in spite of torrential rains, everything was perfect, thanks to the staff and management. They nimbly moved a garden wedding into a beautiful room with large french doors overlooking a garden, giving the impression that we were in a garden yet inside. Food was excellent. All in all -- The Homestead continues to be one of the Grande Dame hotels of America, and one you should visit. Excellent value for price, too!


Richard Silvano 2 years ago – Google

8

Beautiful property which is a bit out of the way. If you are a golfer, you will love it! If you are not a golfer, there are a lot of other activities are available on property. The arcade was great for our 5 yr old grandson, but a bit pricey at $2.00 per game.

My wife reported that Suzy at the spa gave her a wonderful facial. The spa is really clean and the indoor pool was great (it rained almost our entire visit).

The meals are ok, but we, and our guests, found most of the food over-salted, especially the fried food.


Nicole Hawkins 2 years ago – Google

8

Beautiful hotel with old world charm. The lazy river and outdoor pool/ lazy river was perfect for the family. Some of the cosmetics could be improved upon. Biggest negative was that the food was astronomically high priced.....$80 for an adult for a summer kickoff bbq....absurd! I also don't understand why the extra resort fee when every activity added more $ to total bill. Would recommend to family and friends but bring your own drinks and snacks and go to the small local diners for meals!


Patricia Castelli 2 years ago – Google

9

Delightful experience all around. Gorgeous property, incredible staff, wonderful amenities and options for activities. We played golf, had spa treatments, enjoyed the pools, hot tub, natural mineral hot spring and lovely grounds, rested by the fire pit in the evening, ate wonderful food, took the history tour, sat on the front porch in their perfect rocking chairs, loved afternoon tea (wonderful!) and had a relaxing, marvelous visit. Highly recommended.


Mark Gutekunst, DC 2 years ago – Google

8

Hotel staff was terrific. Only major complaint is that Hotel is in need of cosmetic renovation. Carpets, wall coverings, wood work all need renovation and restoration. I know its an old hotel and historic but for the prices I feel more should be done. Not only is there a premium price point but they also charge a resort fee per night. In my opinion things should be better. The building cosmetics need attention. The grounds are beautiful, the staff outstanding. Food was average.


David Murphy 2 years ago – Google

10

We went to the hotel specifically for a two day falconry experience. I would highly recommend you check out this class. Linda, the Master Falconer and Debbie who handles the bookings could not have been more accommodating in spite of the weather challenges. The hotel itself is fantastic with a warm and welcoming staff. Service levels are very high and the food in all 3 restaurants was terrific. Lots to do for guests of any age. We will certainly be back.


Stephanie Henderson 2 years ago – Google

9

This was my first visit to the Omni Homestead Resort for a work conference. I'll definitely be back for a "pleasure" visit.

The staff here provide excellent customer service. Housekeeping does a phenomenal job (especially Yamitza). The guest room and bathroom were spotless, bed was extra comfy. The temperature in the room was perfect - I brought a fan just in case but wasn't really necessary.

We had food from room service, the Lobby Bar and the main dining room. They all exceeded expectations. High tea was also memorable.

The most enjoyable part of the experience, in addition to exploring the impressive property, was meeting Doug and Mike from the Lobby Bar. These two guys know their cocktails, offer great & knowledgeable conversation, have such fun senses of humor and made us want to come back for a non-business visit (ASAP!).

Thanks for making us feel right at home and putting this visit at the top of the list for best business trip in years!


TL Speas 2 years ago – Google

10

The Homestead was absolutely beautiful. The beds are comfortable and the room was well appointed. There were times when I felt transported back in time. I LOVED the afternoon tea. You must participate if you have the chance. It felt so good to sit, listen to the pianist, and sip hot tea. It was an amazing break from my day-to-day craziness. I highly recommend the Homestead to anyone wanting peaceful luxury and a break from it all.


Eric Sundberg 2 years ago – Google

8

Really great old-school hotel shuttle like the one in The Shining. Could not give 5 stars because it's starting to show a little wear though and needs to be refreshed.

The indoor pool is huge (75 feet long and 7 feet deep) and Spa are really nice though. However with two steam rooms and two experiential and chill showers there is no sauna.

Very friendly staff


John Bachman 2 years ago – Google

10

My recent stay at the homestead was an absolute delight. It was not my first visit and I hope it won't be my last. This is a respectable place that caters to a high class clientele and yet at the same time I turn no eyes from the staff when I strut through the main hall in my pajamas or workout pants. This is the pinnacle of professionalism and I appreciate it dearly. I stayed in the owners club villas and if you have the chance I highly recommend it. It offers the amenities of a resort trip with all the comfort of a family owned beach house. Every member of the homestead staff, from shuttle driver to concierge, was an absolute pleasure to interact with. I only wish that my night could have turned into a full weekend.


Vanessa Wagner 2 years ago – Google

7

The building is absolutely beautiful! It was built in 1892 and it still captures the charm of that age. The indoor pool was one of our favorite places to visit aside from the octagon pool in the Serenity Garden. The natural hot spring fed pool was so relaxing! They are a tad bit pricey but that is to be expected at a resort.


Neil Stanton 2 years ago – Google

10

Great place to relax. Polite staff. Lovely countryside. Good food. Golfcourse us fun to play. Highlight was Brian the guide on the gorge hike. What a great guy. Knowledgeable and funny.


Russ Hansen 2 years ago – Google

8

Very cool place. Reminiscent of the great hotels/resorts of the early 1900s with all sorts of activities. The shooting club was very fun and the staff all around the resort were pleasant and helpful.


Shelby Hammock 2 years ago – Google

5

I attended some events here recently. The hotel itself is gorgeous, featuring everything from a theater to a beautiful ballroom and carefully tended outdoor areas. It has everything you would expect for a nice hotel: valet service, attendants to direct you, etc. The prices are insane, though. And you're not even paying for nice things, some of the concessions and such are just twice as expensive as they would be anywhere else. In short: nice place, maybe plan to eat somewhere else.


Safety Freak 2 years ago – Google

5

Very expensive. $6 for a bowl of cereal. Staff was was very nice. $10 a night for parking. Reminds me of the shinning. Room was ok, bathroom was cramped. Room had a big balcony which had great views. The walk to town was short and you can cut through the hotel. Steep ramps on the floor which makes pushing or pulling luggage up was a struggle especially if your older.


Helen Dickinson 3 years ago – Google

10

Love the Omni Homestead. It’s old style Virginia grace and style. The spa and the serenity garden are a MUST. The zip line tour is super fun. The guided hikes and/or the self directed hikes are worth every moment. Whether you are sitting in the grand lobby listening to their pianist while drinking your favorite beverage or playing pool or eating a speculator meal in the main dining room, you will love this place. The breakfast buffet should not be missed.


Kelly Lane 3 years ago – Google

9

A FABULOUS place for vacation! Beautiful resort, fantastic service, wonderful spa and so many activities from zip lining to snowboarding, hiking, horseback riding and my favorite, sporting clays. If you decide to do the shooting range, ask for Frady as your guide! He was great with beginners and experienced shooters alike. Can't wait to go back in April.


Ed Burns 3 years ago – Google

8

Our experience here was amazing. The activities were great and the staff was very friendly. The food was amazing and everything you would expect from a place like this. The one disappointment was the room. For the cost, I would have hoped for some nicer amenities and fixtures in the room.


Joe Burgus 3 years ago – Google

8

Rooms were great. Staff was friendly and very helpful. Location was about an hour SW of Harrisonburg. Room service was excellent. I wish there was more availability of free activities given limited local options.


A Comer Boricua Food & Lifestyle 3 years ago – Google

7

Nice place to visit with your family, friends ,even with coworkers. Neat , clean, nice environment. I personally recommend Jefferson's Rest for nice dinner and Martha's for a casual lunch with friends. And when in Season go to Allegheny Springs (is the restaurant/bar in Pool area) ... delicious menu .
An

webpage.text:
Hot Springs

Mention the Homestead, the Virginian resort in the Allegheny mountains which traces its origins to a hostelry built in 1766, and most people think of "old money." Images of men wearing green sports jackets just back from a round on one of three golf courses or sheet shooting, and ladies enjoying a quiet, respectable afternoon tea at well appointed tables.

There is much about the Homestead today that recalls the time when the resort -- three and one half hours distant from Washington, DC -- was an exclusive playground for blue bloods. For one it is not inexpensive. And some of what the Homestead offers is simply passe -- like the shops offering a variety of clothing few nineties shopper would think of buying.

But most of what is on offer is charming. The fireplaces roaring; the library, thick with books, quiet, and the smell of leather; the staff, attentive and efficient; and the dining, unhurried and elegant.

There is a big part of the Homestead that harkens back to an era when families with money would retire to the country for weeks or even months at a time. It offers guests enjoyment and relaxation on a grand scale. The property has its own power generating station and ski slopes, over 100 miles of riding, hiking, and mountain biking trails, and the famous warm springs, with separate facilities for men and women.


The magnificent entry to the hotel is flanked by long rows of rocking chairs looking out upon the vast, well-manicured grounds. There are tennis courts nearby and the golf pro shop, with a division of golf carts standing ready.

Some visitors no doubt come to the Homestead to sit and rock, but not my family! During our four day stay earlier this spring, we engaged in some very intense vacationing, more typical of the young families that a rejuvenated Homestead, now under new management, is trying to attract.

There is a lot to be said for a vacation getaway that is a reasonable drive from the metropolitan area, where the food and accommodations are great, where adult diversions are plentiful, and where the kids can be kept busy for days on end... and all without need of a car!

The Homestead is such a place. A multi-million dollar renovation aimed at enticing a new generation of vacationing families -- modernizing time worn facilities without a wholesale destruction of the resorts traditional ambiance -- is well underway. To judge by the reaction of my two girls ages 10 and 7, the Homestead is on the right path. And what parent will complain about a vacation where a grand motherly baby sitter [who waited on your table at lunch!] happily shows up at your room so that you can enjoy dinner just for two?

We spent many an hour in the renovated indoor pool, which in early April, was often ours alone. When the pool grew tiresome we headed for the bowling alley nearby, passing on our way the original hot springs pool.

When the weather broke, my wife, along with our toddler Joshua and daughter Morgan, hired a carriage for a long ride along one of the many mountainside trails that cris cross the property. My other daughter Eve and I headed for the horses which had been brought up from the stable for a trail ride.


The Homestead welcomes riders of all abilities and ages. It even has stables available for guests who like to bring their own horses along. Eve has just begun riding lessons, and like many a girl her age, has fallen in love with horses.

The day before our ride, we visited the stables, where she met all the horses and fed carrots to quite a few of them. The stable staff proved very accommodating, and not at all anxious to cut short what was, for my girls, a very exciting outing. Having settled upon one particular beast Eve greeted her the next day as if she were an old friend . With a stable hand in the lead, Eve and I rode for one hour, skirting the golf course, crossing the ski slopes which still retained a hint of winter snow, and trotting up and down gentle, well-marked trails. Eve was in horse heaven. I was pining for a massage.

My wife, however, won the massage sweepstakes. I played with the kids one morning while she worked out on a treadmill in the newly reopened fitness facility. Suitably limber, she headed for the massage table, followed by a facial.

Many of my forty something friends are taking up fly fishing. They sing the praises of the sport as a relaxing way to be outside. I tried it one morning, and I see what they mean. The Homestead offers anglers of all abilities an opportunity to test themselves against the wily trout along a three mile stream running between the Cascades and Lower Cascades golf courses. I spent a couple of hours casting about, and cant say for sure if I got a bite.

----------------------------------------

> ﻿"To judge by the reaction of my two girls ages 10 and 7, the Homestead is on the right path"

After fishing, daughter Morgan and I headed up the 2 mile Cascades Gorge trail. It winds gracefully along the trout stream, climbing over rapids and alongside boulders the size of small buildings. It was a beautiful walk, not too much for a young child, or, Im told, for many of the seniors who visit during summer.

What would a family vacation be without at least one crisis? Ours occurred at the beginning of a bike ride to Lake Moomaw along Richardsons Gorge, five miles distant from the Homestead. The trip was lead by Tray Asbury, owner of Virginia Outdoor Adventures, who offers a variety of bike riding options to Homestead guests. Our first dilemma arose when Morgan proved unable to ride her bike. We should have let her practice at the hotel before staring out some miles away.

"No problem," say Tracy, who simply put Morgan on his bicycle seat and pedaled away. Then it was Joshuas turn. He has always ridden without complaint, seated in a child carrier on the back of my mountain bike. Today, however, he was to sit in one of those two-wheeled enclosed carriers that trail along behind a bike ... and he was having none of it.

It looked as though we were in the running for the shortest bike trip on record. But no, snatching victory from the jaws of defeat we hit upon a solution. As we passed a small country stream, my wife graciously [and not too unhappily] offered stay behind with Joshua while we continued on our way. Morgan settled into the child carrier and off we went, riding for miles along a dirt road which skirted the Jackson River on one side and butted up against hedges of the most extensive wild rhodedendra I have ever seen on the other. Apart form the solitary pickup truck we were alone on this glorious, gentle rural byway.


On our last day at the Homestead, Eve was still intent on indulging her passion for horses. So before we left we mounted up once again, for another -- and not the last I'm sure -- tour around the venerable grounds of the Homestead.

Getting There

The Omni Homestead Resort is nestled in the Allegheny Mountains and is known for its Southern hospitality and charm. The resort has been designated a National Historic Landmark and makes up most of the city of Hot Springs, Virginia.

From New York - 450 miles, 8 hours driving time


Take I-78 West to I-81 South. On I-81 South, take Exit #220, which will put you on Route 262 North. Take Route 262 to Route 254 West (the Parkersburg Pike exit). Route 254 becomes Route 42 South and then Route 42 becomes Route 39 West. Take Route 39 to U.S. 220 South and follow U.S. 220 south to the Homestead.

From Philadelphia - 340 miles, 6 hours driving time


Take I-76 West to I-81 South. On I-81 South, take Exit #220, which will put you on Route 262 North. Take Route 262 to Route 254 West (the Parkersburg Pike exit). Route 254 becomes Route 42 South and then Route 42 becomes Route 39 West. Take Route 39 to U.S. 220 South and follow U.S. 220 south to the Homestead.

From Washington, D.C. - 210 miles, 4 hours driving time

webpage.text:
The Omni Homestead Resort

Historic resort in Virginia, US


United States historic place


The Homestead
U.S. National Register of Historic Places
U.S. National Historic Landmark
Virginia Landmarks Register

Front view of The Homestead Resort
Location within Virginia
Location              US 220, Hot Springs, Virginia
Coordinates           37°59′43.70″N 79°49′46.72″W﻿ / ﻿37.9954722°N 79.8296444°W﻿ /
                      37.9954722; -79.8296444
Area                  2,300 acres (930 ha)
Built                 1892
Architect             Multiple
Architectural style   Queen Anne, Greek Revival, Colonial Revival
NRHP reference No.    84003494[1]
VLR No.               008-0025
Significant dates
Added to NRHP         May 3, 1984
Designated NHL        July 17, 1991[2]
Designated VLR        March 20, 1984[3]

The Omni Homestead Resort is a luxury resort in Hot Springs, Virginia, United States, in the middle of the Allegheny Mountains. The area has the largest hot springs in the Commonwealth, and the resort is also known for its championship golf courses, which have hosted several national tournaments. The resort also includes an alpine ski resort; founded in 1959, it is the oldest in Virginia. The resort has been designated a National Historic Landmark; it has a history extending more than two and a half centuries. The Omni Homestead Resort is a member of Historic Hotels of America[4] the official program of the National Trust for Historic Preservation.


History

In 1766, Thomas Bullitt built a lodge on the site, which is considered the founding of The Homestead. It has hosted vacationers ever since, including twenty-three U.S. presidents.

The modern resort dates from 1888–1892, when a group of investors headed by J. P. Morgan bought the business and started rebuilding it from the ground up. The original hotel buildings burned down in 1901, caused by a fire in the bakery. The main Homestead hotel was constructed afterwards, one wing a year, with the main lobby reconstructed in 1902.

Many American Presidents and influential people were Homestead guests. William Howard Taft spent July and August 1908 at the Homestead, working and relaxing before the final campaign push, as did outgoing President Theodore Roosevelt, for a short period of time.[5] Other notable guests included cartoonist Carl E. Schultze of Foxy Grandpa fame.

From December 1941 until June 1942, following the United States' entry into World War II, the Homestead served as a high-end internment camp for 785 Japanese diplomats and their families until they could be exchanged through neutral channels for their American counterparts.[6][7] The diplomats were later transferred to the Greenbrier Hotel in West Virginia.[8][9]

In 1943, during World War II, The Homestead hosted an important conference of the United Nations in which was implemented the foundation of the Food and Agriculture Organization.[10][11]

In 1993, The Homestead was purchased by Club Resorts, the same company which owned the Pinehurst Resort in North Carolina. In 2006, Club Resorts and its parent company ClubCorp, Inc. were acquired by a private-equity group led by KSL Capital Partners. KSL Resorts assumed management of The Homestead at this time. KSL sold the resort to Omni Hotels in 2013 and it was renamed The Omni Homestead Resort.[12] From October 2021 to October 2023, the entire resort underwent a complete renovation, costing over $150 million.[13]

The Homestead was designated a National Historic Landmark in 1991. Associated with The Homestead are the Homestead Dairy Barns, listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2007.[1]


Golf

The Homestead features two golf courses. The club is sometimes referred to as Virginia Hot Springs Golf & Tennis Club. The area produced an 82-time winner on the PGA Tour in the late Sam Snead.

The Old Course started as a six-hole layout in 1892, and the first tee is the oldest in continuous use in the United States.[14] It was expanded to 18 holes by 1901, and Donald Ross redesigned it in 1913. The course has been modified at various times since, and the current course has six par 5s and six par 3s.

The Cascades Course is the most famous of the two, and is usually ranked among the top 100 U.S. courses by both Golf Digest and GOLF Magazine. The Cascades is the course used when hosting national tournaments, including seven United States Golf Association championships. It was designed by William S. Flynn (who was also a main architect for Shinnecock Hills), and opened in 1923.

There was formerly a third course, the Lower Cascades, which was designed by Robert Trent Jones Sr. in 1963. It hosted qualifying rounds for the U.S. Amateur tournament. It was closed following the 2012 season.

Famed PGA Tour champion Sam Snead lived in or near Hot Springs all of his life, and served for decades as the Homestead's golf pro. Snead also holds the course record of 60, which he set in 1983 at the age of 71.


Tournaments

 * 1928 U.S. Women's Amateur, won by Glenna Collett
 * 1932 National Intercollegiate Championship, won by Yale (team) and Johnny Fischer (individual)
 * 1966 Curtis Cup, won by the United States over Great Britain & Ireland 13-5
 * 1967 U.S. Women's Open, won by Catherine Lacoste
 * 1980 U.S. Senior Amateur, won by William C. Campbell
 * 1988 U.S. Amateur, won by Eric Meeks
 * 1994 U.S. Women's Amateur, won by Wendy Ward
 * 1995 Merrill Lynch Shoot-Out Championship (Senior PGA Tour)
 * 1996 Merrill Lynch Shoot-Out Championship (Senior PGA Tour)
 * 2000 U.S. Mid-Amateur, won by Greg Puga
 * 2004 NCAA Division I Men's Championship, won by California (team) and Ryan Moore (UNLV)(individual)
 * 2009 USGA Senior Women's Amateur Championship[15]
 * 2023 U.S. Senior Women's Amateur[16]
 * 2025 U.S. Senior Women's Amateur[17][18]


Spa

The Homestead offers spa services to guests including massages, facial treatments, manicures and pedicures, and stays in the Serenity Garden, where guests can soak in pools fed by natural geothermal springs. Also located in the spa is the hotel's fitness center and indoor pool, open to any guests of the resort.[19]

Another location operated by the Homestead is the Warm Springs Pools, geothermal springs housed in historic structures. Guests of the hotel and day guests can book hour-long sessions to soak in the pools. The resort provides shuttle rides from the hotel to Warm Springs.[20]


Recreation

The Homestead offers many activities to guests, including a two-acre waterpark with a lazy river and water slides, mini golf, tennis, kayaking, fly fishing, horseback riding, skeet shooting, archery, zip lining, guided hikes, and lawn games.[21]

The resort originally featured an Olympic sized skating rink that closed when the Zamboni became unusable. In 2008, the Homestead built a new 30 X 20 foot ice skating rink in time for the 2008-2009 winter season. In 2013, the ice rink was relocated to Allegheny Springs, adjacent to the outdoor pool.


Ski resort

The ski area at The Homestead was opened in 1959;[22] it is the oldest ski resort in Virginia, and was developed by Sepp Kober, known as 'The Father of Southern Skiing'.[23] Natural snowfall on the ski hill is supplemented by snowmaking equipment and groomed by machines for optimal ski and snowboard experience.

The resort's main and only northwest-facing slope is serviced by three lifts, including a double chairlift which accesses the intermediate and advanced terrain at the top of the hill, and two surface lifts which serve the beginner terrain at the bottom and at the tubing hill. The chairlift has a mid-mountain drop-off station which accesses intermediate terrain. The resort offers a variety of other winter activities including snow tubing.


Statistics:

Elevation

 * Summit Elevation: 3,200 ft (980 m)
 * Base Elevation: 2,500 ft (760 m)
 * Vertical Rise: 700 feet (210 m)

Terrain

 * Skiable area: 40 acres (0.16 km2)
 * Runs: 10 total
   * 35% beginner
   * 55% intermediate
   * 10% advanced
 * Longest run: 4,200 feet (1,300 m)
 * Annual snowfall: 50 inches (1.3 m)

Resort capacity

 * Lift system: 3 lifts total
   * 1 double chairlift
   * 1 rope tows
   * I conveyor
 * Uphill lift capacity: 1,143 skiers/hour
 * Snowmaking: 100% of trails


March 2009 shooting

On March 21, 2009, two resort employees were shot and killed in the hotel kitchen;[24] the community of Hot Springs was briefly locked down under code red procedures as a security precaution.[25] Authorities identified fellow employee Beacher Ferrel Hackney as a suspect in the killings.[26] The slayings were the first homicides in Bath County since 1983.[27] On September 2, 2012, Hackney's remains, clothing, some personal possessions, and pistol were found near the Homestead's Lower Cascades golf course.[28] The cause of death has not been determined.[29]


Gallery

 * The Homestead as viewed from one of its golf courses, the Old Course
 * Fireworks on the lawn to celebrate memorial day
 * Christmas Tree lighting in the Great Hall of the Homestead
 * Interior of the Warm Springs Pools, historic geothermal spa buildings operated by the Homestead in the town of Warm Springs, Virginia
 * Indoor pool of the Homestead, located in the spa
 * 'Mini Cascades' miniature golf course

resultats_lens.texte_contexte: The Omni Homestead Resort est un complexe hôtelier de luxe historique situé à Hot Springs, en Virginie, au milieu des montagnes Allegheny. Fondé en 1766 par Thomas Bullitt qui y construisit un pavillon, le site moderne s'est développé entre 1888 et 1892 sous l'impulsion d'investisseurs menés par J.P. Morgan, après un incendie en 1901. Il a accueilli de nombreux présidents américains, a servi brièvement de camp d'internement pour des diplomates japonais en 1941-1942, et a accueilli une conférence des Nations unies en 1943. Il est inscrit au Registre national des lieux historiques et désigné comme National Historic Landmark.
